Synopsis:
A mud mephit called Boney who works with his earth elemental wife Stoney to sell statues in the circus.

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_Circus_Sculptor.json: Boney is a mud mephit stall‑vendor at the circus who teams with his earth‑elemental wife Stoney to carve and sell statues; the troupe is packing up soon, so purchases feel time‑sensitive. Off‑screen Stoney quietly works in a nearby workshop and is shy and protective of her creative process, while Boney mans the front, cheerfully hawking wares and trying to enthuse customers. He can be playful and tactless—mocking looks or joking about an adventurer’s purse—more smarmy than cruel, and he’ll both upsell and offer leniency if someone can’t pay. Players may request custom pieces (e.g., a camp statue) or simply browse; Boney’s tone shifts from excited to dejected depending on interest, and he won’t want Stoney disturbed when she’s at her “creative zenith.”
- WYR_Circus_Checkpoint.json: The dialog on the entrance to the extraplanar circus, where the player sees a ghoul sniffing entering customers - new measures because of the recent murders nearby. The player can pay an entrance fee and go and see the circus.
- WYR_Circus_EntranceGuard.json: One-liner dialog for a circus worker on the checkpoint after the player is allowed to enter. He has a friendly circus ghoul with him to check on the entering customers.
- WYR_Circus_Ringmaster.json: Main dialog for the ringmaster - a necromancer lady and the owner of the circus. She has her own tent where she trains dancing skeleton troupe, but after combat with Dribbles she runs to the combat scene and will ask player some questions.
- WYR_Circus_Merchant.json: Dialog for the circus kobold merchant, who sells weird magical items and shady stuff. He feels like the shady drug dealer on the corner who is high on his own merchandise. In this dialogue, after the dribbles fight, you can also buy dribble's hand off him (for a ridiculously high price.)

context: Boney is a mud mephit who runs a stall at the circus, selling statues carved by his earth‑elemental wife, Stoney. Off‑screen Stoney works quietly in a nearby workshop; she’s very shy and protective of her process and Boney will not want her disturbed when she’s at her “creative zenith.” The troupe is packing up soon, so purchases feel time‑sensitive; Boney alternates between cheerful, smarmy salesmanship (teasing about looks or purses), upselling, and offering leniency if a customer can’t pay. Players can browse wares or request custom pieces (for example, a camp statue), and Boney’s tone shifts from excited to dejected based on interest.
